title: Japan's Budget Restaurant Saizeriya Raises Prices
paragraphs: With food prices rising around the world, finding a cheap meal isn't always easy. But in Japan, one restaurant chain is famous for keeping its prices low.
Saizeriya, a popular Italian restaurant chain, sells its famous Milano doria for just 300 yen (about $1.90), while a Margherita pizza costs only 400 yen (about $2.50).
Or at least, that's what they used to cost.
But now, Saizeriya is increasing its prices for the first time in six years.
On October 29, Saizeriya prices increased by an average of 6%, and some restaurants increased prices by as much as 10%.

It's the company's first general price increase since 1998. Saizeriya did make some small changes in 2020, but those were intended to reduce the need for coins and change during the COVID-19 pandemic.
Over the years, Saizeriya has found different ways to save money and keep its prices low. For example, it has its own vegetable farms and factories, and has even tried using robots to serve food.
But these efforts are no longer enough, as higher food and energy costs have made it difficult to avoid price increases.
At a press conference in October, Saizeriya CEO Hideharu Matsutani said the price increase was "regrettable."
But after hearing the announcement, many people shared messages on social media in support of Saizeriya.

One customer told The Japan Times that Saizeriya's meals have been so cheap that eating there can cost less than cooking at home, and that most people are just surprised the company has kept its prices so low for so long.
And even with the higher prices, Saizeriya still wants to keep its food affordable.
At the press conference, Matsutani said that if the company finds another way to make meals cheaper, he'll take it.
